title: New EWTN Exorcism Series Explores the Church's Battle Against Satan
excerpt: Three-part ‘In Jesus’ Name’ explores the dangers of the occult, the Church’s ministry of exorcism and Christ’s victory over evil.
content:
Three-part ‘In Jesus’ Name’ explores the dangers of the occult, the Church’s ministry of exorcism and Christ’s victory over evil.

During his first exorcism, Father Dan Reehil looked at an image of Our Lady of Guadalupe and said to the woman who was suffering terribly, “Please turn to your Mother.” 

The woman followed the priest’s directive — and was freed.

Father Reehil’s recollection is just one of the many stories told in the new EWTN three-part documentary series In Jesus’ Name.

From EWTN Studios and Cumberland Creative, In Jesus’ Name, streaming on EWTN+ Oct. 28-30, explores the spiritual battle for the human soul. Experienced exorcists, theologians and survivors of demonic oppression reveal how evil operates and enters human lives — and how it can be overcome in Jesus’ name.

“The recounting of the rituals and behaviors they practiced, which opened the door to that evil in their life, is meant to reveal and expose the deceptions of Satan, who uses fear and allurement to draw people away from God,” explains Father Reehil, a pastor and diocesan exorcist in the Diocese of Nashville, national director of Radio Maria USA and host of Battle Ready with Fr. Dan Reehil, in the series.

“The purpose of this documentary,” he continues, “is not to glorify or overly dramatize the work of the devil. It’s meant to educate you on the reality of spiritual warfare, which affects all of us every day, whether you believe in it or not, so that you may be aware and equipped to arm yourself against the enemy of your soul with all the weapons that Christ our Lord has given his Church, both ordinary and extraordinary.”

The continued need for exorcism does not surprise Charles Fraune, founder of Slaying Dragons Apostolate and author of Slaying Dragons: What Exorcists See & What We Should Know (Slaying Dragons Press).

“The gradual decline of cultures has accelerated so much in recent decades that only a clear and undeniable presentation of the consequences of sin is able to stir man to his senses,” he told the Register. “Even those who love evil still crave the good — it is how we are made. In their consciences, all men and women desire, deeply, to be convicted about their sins — to know what is right and wrong. The shocking truths communicated through a knowledge of the Church’s work in exorcisms has proven to be a powerful means of converting people back to God.”

A Historical Look

The series makes clear that the Church carries on this ministry of exorcism today, as it has done from biblical times.

The opening episode, “Non Serviam,” explores the origins and reality of evil — how demons operate, what they pursue and how they try to influence humanity. The insights cement the reality of spiritual warfare. That warfare is grounded in biblical teaching (such as Mark 1, Luke 8 and 10, and Matthew 10), beginning with Jesus driving out demons and giving the apostles the same authority.

Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, who has significant experience with exorcism ministry, points out in the series, “The rite of exorcism, like many things in the Church, grew up with time. The earliest extant forms of exorcism were the Name. That’s all. Jesus. Even the early Fathers of the Church, in their writings, make reference to the power of the Name.”

The Name delivers indeed.

“Exorcism was one of the principal works that Christ performed during his ministry on earth,” Fraune told the Register. “The devil and his angels are always pursuing us, and Christ is always seeking to defend us from the devil’s activity, to heal us, enlighten us, and raise us up to divine life.”

Beware the Devil

The second episode, “Swinging Doors,” examines pathways that can open the door to spiritual oppression and allow demonic influence to take root in a person’s life. Firsthand stories stress the dangers of the occult, the need for proper spiritual authority and pastoral care, and how the Church identifies and responds to spiritual attacks or possession. 

Viewers hear from people who offer insights into their newfound lives in Christ after being rescued. Their stories of deliverance from Wicca and other occult practices should convince viewers what can happen once they open the door to such darkness.

The final episode, “Deliver Us From Evil,” looks at the role of human free will in the spiritual battle between good and evil. Testimonies show that exorcism does not stand alone but is part of a deeper path of faith and conversion. Hope is the overriding message.

Detailing the Dangers

This three-part series will open the eyes of people dangerously drawn to the occult, which has been made by some celebrities to appear innocuous. But the series makes clear that the opposite is true — it is most harmful. 

At the same time, the calm explanations by Father Reehil, newly retired exorcist Father Vincent Lampert and other contributors clearly show how to avoid that dark road and keep to the right path.

One of the episodes features a clinical psychologist who works for his diocese by evaluating possible candidates for major exorcism. Psychological assessment is always part of the process, because not every struggle is demonic in origin.

Viewers also learn how demons act and that their methods fall within two categories: ordinary temptation and extraordinary influence. The episodes focus most on extraordinary attacks that involve oppression, obsession, infestation or, in rare cases, possession.

Our Lady’s Aid

The Mother of God has her role too.

The Blessed Mother is essential in exorcism, as Father Reehil’s first exorcism well attests. 

As Fraune told the Register, “Every single action Jesus Christ performed on earth as the ‘God-man’ undid the victories Satan had celebrated for millennia. By uniting the Blessed Virgin Mary to his own work of redemption, Jesus Christ exerts this same power, this same undoing of the kingdom of Satan, through her.” 

“As one singularly gifted by a plenitude of grace and holiness, without any stain or defect, Mary cooperated perfectly with Christ's work,” he observed. “The Church militant depends upon her most among all of the many intercessors in the Church triumphant, and this has been seen with great evidence in the work of exorcism.”

The Reality

Father Lampert, who started as the designated exorcist for the Archdiocese of Indianapolis more than 20 years ago, explains in the series how the Church “in the ministry of exorcism wants to pull back the curtain so that we can see Satan for who he truly is” and “realize that he is nothing to be afraid of.” He says the devil always tries to portray himself as something more than he is.

Such counsel encourages viewers, who also learn that guardian angels are more powerful than Satan.

“Yes, the devil is real, powerful and active, but he’s so weak. If you are holy, if you are saintly, the devil is afraid of you. The dog is on a leash. You have a healthy respect for the works of darkness and the evil one in his abilities. And you have no need to fear him because we have one greater in the Person of Jesus Christ,” a voiceover explains.

Victory comes through celebrating the Church’s sacramental life, going to confession and Mass, receiving Communion, praying, and reading and knowing the Word of God. 

“If we’re doing these things, the devil is on the run,” says Father Lampert.

“Remember that the devil was defeated in the cross of Christ 2,000 years ago,” observes the late theologian Paul Thigpen, author of the Manual for Spiritual Warfare. “The devil was decisively defeated. These are the mop-up operations. And as long as we are with Christ, who triumphed over the devil, then his victory becomes our victory.”

He adds, “There are so many other people who have suffered these things. But the Church wants to help you. And not only that, we’re part of a vast army of holy ones that are part of the victory of the Lord. The Lord himself is our commander. ... The battle’s already won and you’re not alone.”

WATCH

In Jesus’ Name will stream Oct. 28, 29 and 30 on EWTN+.

Viewer discretion is advised because of some scenes and accounts from those previously affected. Music reinforcing the subject matter is used throughout.
